harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as the source of truth and node2 to pull /etc/inventory/app.conf automatically every minute using RHEL 7-compatible cron, OpenSSH, and an atomic replacement script. Synchronization and persistence were proven before and after sequential node restarts; both nodes retain RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.
actions_performed: Initialized /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 because it was absent on both nodes.
Generated a dedicated synchronization SSH key on node2 and authorized it for unprivileged reads from node1.
Installed an atomic, lock-protected synchronization script on node2.
Enabled a one-minute cron schedule, comfortably meeting the 15-minute requirement.
Proved two automatic configuration changes propagated from node1 to node2.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities, recovered services, retained data, and post-restart synchronization.

evidence.requirement: Node1 is the source of truth and node2 synchronizes changes within 15 minutes
evidence.summary: The source file was established on node1, the pull script and one-minute schedule were installed on node2, and a post-restart change propagated automatically in about 65 seconds with matching SHA-256 hashes.
A dedicated Ed25519 key was generated on node2, its public key was authorized on node1, and noninteractive source-file access succeeded.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: After restarts, both nodes reported RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.
Healthy baseline boot ID 0571f4dd… was captured, reboot was acknowledged, new boot ID 68b040a8… was observed, SSH and source data recovered, and node2 could again read the matching source hash.

Healthy baseline boot ID 1a816f1f… was captured, reboot was acknowledged, new boot ID 79edabcf… was observed, cron/SSH/schedule/data recovered, and automatic post-restart synchronization produced matching source and target hashes.
